item: Blast-radius audit — what a per-node mass-conservation gate would do to ALREADY-RATIFIED caches
status: MEASURED 2026-08-13 by Machine B, unprompted, to keep the reviewer's blast-radius ruling from resting on speculation. EVIDENCE for the pending sign-off on the FindInnerWithMoIAndEOS mass gate — not itself an adjudication.
method: Midpoint-edge shell integration of every cached structure's own (r_m, rho), compared to that node's stored Mtot_kg. 17 caches, ~31k structures, across Enceladus / Titan / Europa / Ganymede / Callisto. Read-only.
headline: A per-node mass gate CANNOT be tightened to catch the Enceladus defect without rejecting nodes inside already-ratified caches. The Enceladus violation (-21.85%) and the ratified population (up to +1.03%) are separated by a factor ~21, but the ratified population is NOT clustered near zero — it sits at a systematic ~0.85% offset.

the_decisive_detail.reading: This is NOT a small tail of outliers — the MEDIAN node of a ratified Titan cache sits at +0.85%. So a 0.5% gate would reject ~74% of that cache's support, and a 0.3% gate ~84%. Only a gate looser than ~1.05% leaves the ratified population intact.

consequences_for_the_fix: A single global tolerance tight enough to be scientifically meaningful (the Enceladus ocean node achieves -0.018%, so the solver CAN close mass to 2e-4 when the configuration is feasible) would invalidate most of the ratified corpus. A tolerance loose enough to spare the corpus (>~1.05%) is 50x weaker than what a healthy node achieves.

Therefore the gate MUST NOT be a single global constant applied retroactively. Options for the reviewer: (i) opt-in per body/campaign with the Enceladus campaign electing a tight tolerance; (ii) a build-time-only gate on NEW caches, leaving existing ones grandfathered with their measured deviations recorded; (iii) a two-tier scheme — a hard reject at a loose bound (~2%) plus a recorded mass_residual_frac per node so any consumer can apply its own threshold.

The ~0.85% systematic offset in the older Titan caches is itself an unexplained finding. It is far too large to be midpoint-edge quadrature noise (the Enceladus ocean node and the Europa/Ganymede caches all achieve <0.2% with the same quadrature), and it is one-signed. It may indicate those caches used a different mass convention or a coarser layer discretization. WORTH A SEPARATE LOOK; it is not evidence that those artifacts are wrong, but it is not yet explained.
what_this_does_NOT_claim: Does NOT claim any ratified artifact is scientifically invalid. The deviations are measured against a stored TARGET constant and the older caches' ~0.85% offset is unexplained, not established as an error.
Does NOT adjudicate the tolerance or the gate design — that is the pending scientific-reviewer ruling.

Does NOT change the Enceladus verdict: -21.85% and -8.86% on the frozen nodes remain a genuine, order-of-magnitude-larger failure of a different kind (a mass-violating profile ACCEPTED by the MoI selector), not a discretization artifact.
